facts.raw_span: 1-month history of insidious-onset right lower abdominal pain
lifelong non-pitting edema of the left leg extending to the labia majora
afebrile
blood pressure was 110/80 mmHg
firm, non-tender, mobile mass measuring approximately 12 cm × 10 cm in the right lower quadrant
bimanual pelvic examination confirmed a right adnexal mass
carcinoembryonic antigen 1.14 ng/mL
lactate dehydrogenase 251 U/L
Transvaginal ultrasound showed multiple uterine fibroids and a large hypoechoic lesion in the right adnexa
Contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen and pelvis revealed a well-marginated thin-walled solid-cystic lesion measuring 16.1 × 7.9 × 8.1 cm in the abdominopelvic region
a provisional diagnosis of a malignant ovarian tumor
double inferior vena cava was identified, with the left cava draining via the left renal vein to the right-sided cava

concepts.why: The patient's transvaginal ultrasound and contrast-enhanced CT scans revealed a large hypoechoic lesion in the right adnexa, which is consistent with an ovarian serous cystadenoma.
The patient's transvaginal ultrasound showed multiple uterine fibroids, which are a common finding in women of reproductive age.
The patient presented with lifelong non-pitting edema of the left leg, which is consistent with lymphedema.

aliases: Congenital Anomaly of Inferior Vena Cava
concepts.why: The patient's contrast-enhanced CT scan revealed a double inferior vena cava, which is a rare congenital anomaly.
The patient's provisional diagnosis was a malignant ovarian tumor, which is a possible explanation for the large hypoechoic lesion in the right adnexa.
The patient's contrast-enhanced CT scan revealed a double inferior vena cava, which is a type of venous anomaly.
The patient's lifelong non-pitting edema of the left leg may be associated with chronic inflammation, although the exact cause is unclear.
Although the patient's serology for filarial infection was negative, the possibility of an infectious disease cannot be entirely ruled out.
